subject: Pilot -> Multi-region scale: procurement windows, canary routing & burst cadence
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Miles <jmiles@atlasmed.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scheduling + procurement window options

Hi Jacob —

Great chatting yesterday. Per our call, AtlasMed is ready to run the 6-week pilot in us-west and then stage a phased region add (us-east -> eu-west) if metrics look good. To make the handoff to Ops and Procurement clean, I sketched a short mutual-action checklist so NetOps can book maintenance windows and Procurement can align on billing commit cadence.

High-level asks from Redwood:
- Confirm the preferred procurement window for pilot pre-pay vs PO (30 days vs 60 days).
- NetOps maintenance blackout windows (so we avoid scheduled infra work during canary).
- Successful canary routing: pilot traffic can be pinned to a single availability slice for 72 hours, then cross-region test for 24 hours.

I'll attach a lightweight spreadsheet with recommended procurement timeboxes and a proposed canary sequence for your NetOps team. If that looks good, Monica will follow up with the technical gating and burst-credit cadence.

Thanks — talk soon,
Jonas
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: atlasmed-procurement-windows.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Jacob Miles <jmiles@atlasmed.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Rao <anita@atlasmed.com>, AtlasMed IT <it@atlasmed.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scheduling + procurement window options

Jonas —

Thanks for the summary and the spreadsheet. We prefer PO/Net30 for the pilot, but Procurement may be able to do a 60-day approval for a short-term committed credit if that helps acceleration. NetOps team asked to avoid Thursdays 02:00-06:00 UTC (weekly maintenance).

A couple of specifics from our side:
- Can you confirm how burst credits would be billed during the pilot? We need an estimate for our finance approvers.
- For the canary, we'd like to start with 5% production-like traffic routed to Redwood, then ramp to 20% after 48h if no regressions.

Looping in Anita (security/compliance) — she will own the SLA exception request if we need emergency burst beyond committed credits.

—Jacob
Director of Platform Engineering, AtlasMed
[Attachment: None]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Miles <jmiles@atlasmed.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scheduling + procurement window options

Jacob —

Perfect, PO Net30 aligns well. On burst credits: for the pilot we can provide a capped burst-credit pool at no additional charge (up to X GPU-hours); usage beyond that will be invoiced at the pilot rate discussed in the spreadsheet. Monica included a detailed billing cadence doc in the attachments in case Procurement wants line items.

Proposed canary sequence (we can adapt):
1) Day 0–3: 5% traffic to Redwood slice A (single AZ) — smoke + perf checks.
2) Day 4–5: 20% traffic to Redwood slice A (cross-AZ warmup).
3) Day 6: cross-region validation (us-east) for 24h at 10% before scale decision.

NetOps blackout logged — avoid Thursdays 02:00-06:00 UTC. We'll mark that in the mutual action doc.

Monica — can you upload the canary routing note and the burst-credit cadence file to the shared Drive and call out any NetOps ops hooks we need?

Jonas
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Miles <jmiles@atlasmed.com>, AtlasMed IT <it@atlasmed.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scheduling + procurement window options

Hi Jacob / AtlasMed IT team —

Attaching the ops checklist and the burst-credit cadence workbook. Summary of technical gating below:

Ops checklist (high level):
- Test matrix: perf (p95 latency), error rate, token-cost delta per route.
- Canary routing: use header-based routing toggles; we recommend toggling at the ingress LB so rollback is instant.
- KV/prefix priming: run a pre-warm job for 1 hour with representative queries before the canary goes live.
- Autoscaling config: min replicas = 2 (pilot slice), max replicas = 12; target p95 = 300ms.
- Burst policy: automatic bursting up to 2x baseline for 10 minutes; emergency manual burst (operator) with approval for up to 8x for up to 2 hours.

Billing/cadence summary (see attached burst-credit-cadence.xlsx):
- Pilot: Redwood issues an initial 1000-credit pool (no charge).
- Overage: billable at pilot rate per-credit, invoiced monthly.
- Post-pilot: reserve commit options available; we recommend a 3-month bridge if you need smoothing before a full committed pool.

NetOps hooks: please provide an API endpoint for your ingress LB team to accept the header-based routing toggle (we provided example curl in the Drive doc). Also confirm the maintenance blackout windows we discussed (Thursdays 02:00-06:00 UTC).

Attachments: atlasmed-procurement-windows.xlsx, redwood-canary-routing-notes.pdf, burst-credit-cadence.xlsx

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick tech call to walk through the checklist.

Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-canary-routing-notes.pdf (docs)]

From: Anita Rao <anita@atlasmed.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Jacob Miles <jmiles@atlasmed.com>, AtlasMed IT <it@atlasmed.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scheduling + procurement window options

Monica / Jonas —

Thanks for the checklist. A couple security questions before we formalize the canary:
- Emergency burst SLA exception: what logs/audit trails do you generate when manual burst is invoked? We need to capture traceability for compliance.
- Data residency for logs: during cross-region validation, where are access logs stored?

If Redwood can provide an event-level audit (user/operator id, timestamp, duration, reason code) for manual bursts and store logs in our EU bucket (for the EU phase), we can fast-track the exception approval.

Anita Rao
Head of Security & Compliance, AtlasMed

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita@atlasmed.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot scheduling + procurement window options

Anita —

We can provide the exact event-level audit you requested for manual bursts: operator id, start/end timestamps, duration, reason code, and pre/post capacity snapshot. Logs for the EU-validation phase can be pushed to your EU S3 (or GCS) bucket via our secure replication; we include an encrypted delivery proof and retention metadata. I'll drop the formal SLA-exception template to the Drive folder and link the DocuSign when ready.

DocuSign preview: https://app.docusign.com/preview/DEAL-ATLAS-78452

If this meets your gating, Jonas — can we lock the kickoff for week of Apr 26? Procurement Net30 path looks feasible from your side; procurement please confirm.

Rishi
Director, Product — Onboarding & Reliability
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLA-exception-template.docx (document)]
thread_summary: Mutual-action planning thread between Redwood (Sales + Solutions) and AtlasMed for a 6-week pilot that will scale multi-region if metrics pass. Covers procurement windows (PO Net30 preferred), NetOps blackout times, a staged canary routing plan, autoscaling/burst policy details, billing/cadence for burst credits, and security gating for manual burst SLA exceptions. Attachments include procurement spreadsheet, canary routing notes, and burst-credit cadence workbook. DocuSign preview and SLA-exception template noted for next steps.
